articles.title: 'In politics, I don't trust anybody': Trump says when asked about Netanyahu
articles.summary:
'In politics, I don't trust anybody': Trump says when asked about Netanyahu

US President Donald Trump has said he does not trust anybody in politics when asked directly whether he trusts Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, weeks before Israel’s parliamentary election.

In an interview with Newsmax’s “Finnerty” on Thursday, host Rob Finnerty asked whether he trusted Netanyahu. “I don’t trust anybody, honestly,” Trump replied.

“I don’t trust anybody. In the world of politics, I don’t trust anybody,” Trump repeated. He did not say whether he had any particular concerns about Netanyahu, with whom he has kept a close political and military partnership.

Asked whether he planned to get involved in the 27 October election, in which Netanyahu is seeking another term, Trump said: "Well, they'd like me to be. Yeah, they'd like me to be." 

He added: “I’ve had a very good relationship with him. We’ve had good success together.”

Trump has previously held back from endorsing Netanyahu. In a Time interview published on 1 October, he said his “primary thing” was to help defend Israel.

articles.title: Iraq appoints leader from Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq as deputy PM
articles.summary:
Iraq appoints leader from Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq as deputy PM

Iraq’s parliament has approved Laith al-Khazali, a senior figure from the Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq movement, as a deputy prime minister.

The United States designated the group a "foreign terrorist organisation" in 2020.

Khazali is the brother of the movement’s leader, Qais al-Khazali. Washington designated both brothers as "specially designated global terrorists", citing attacks including a 2007 assault that killed five US soldiers. The US Treasury also sanctioned them in 2019 over the killing of protesters in Iraq.

Lawmakers on Thursday approved three deputy prime ministers and 11 ministers, completing Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The appointments include Nayef al-Shammari as defence minister and Yasir al-Maliki as interior minister.

Zaidi's government has pledged economic reforms, anti-corruption measures and efforts to strengthen state institutions — but faces steep challenges, including rebuilding an economy battered by regional instability, tackling endemic corruption, and reining in Iran-allied armed groups, according to Reuters.

articles.title: Trump weighs new Iran strikes while insisting talks continue
articles.summary:
Trump weighs new Iran strikes while insisting talks continue

US President Donald Trump has said he is weighing fresh strikes on Iran without nuclear weapons or ground troops, while insisting negotiations with Tehran were under way.

Asked on Newsmax’s “Finnerty” on Thursday about reports he is considering the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb, the “mother of all bombs”, possibly after the 3 November midterms, Trump said it is “not nuclear at all”. He called it “just an extremely large bomb”. 

CNN reported that the US military has drawn up plans to use the roughly 21,600-pound MOAB against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites if Trump orders renewed combat. 

Asked if that would involve American ground troops, he said: “No, I don’t see that.” He said that withdrawing now risks having to “do it again” within a year, reiterating "Iran must never get a nuclear weapon".

Trump predicted the war “will be over very soon”, adding that “they are negotiating with us”. He said the end would come “one way or the other”.

“They’ve asked us to please stop. And we do, because we’re negotiating with them,” he said.

archive.security_status_cs: Napětí v regionu prudce eskaluje kvůli přímým vojenským hrozbám vůči Íránu, incidentům v Hormuzském průlivu a politickým tlakům na Libanon. Vnitřní nestabilita v Izraeli a Gaze spolu s kybernetickými útoky na novináře nadále prohlubují bezpečnostní rizika.
archive.security_status_en: Regional tensions are escalating sharply due to direct military threats against Iran, incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, and political pressure on Lebanon. Internal instability in Israel and Gaza, alongside cyberattacks on journalists, continue to deepen security risks.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující eskalaci rétoriky kolem Íránu a zvýšenou ostražitost v oblasti námořní dopravy v Zálivu. Diplomatické tlaky na Izrael a Libanon budou nadále zatěžovat regionální stabilitu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued escalation of rhetoric surrounding Iran and heightened vigilance in Gulf shipping lanes are expected. Diplomatic pressures on Israel and Lebanon will continue to strain regional stability.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu zůstává vysoce napjatá v důsledku hrozeb nových amerických úderů na Írán, politických změn v Iráku a přetrvávající nestability v Gaze a Libanonu. Kritická infrastruktura a námořní trasy v Zálivu čelí rostoucím hrozbám po útocích na energetická zařízení v Sýrii a lodní dopravu.
archive.security_status_en: The regional security situation remains highly tense due to threats of fresh US strikes on Iran, political shifts in Iraq, and persistent instability in Gaza and Lebanon. Critical infrastructure and Gulf shipping lanes face rising threats following attacks on energy assets in Syria and maritime shipping.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další eskalaci rétoriky mezi USA a Íránem a zvýšené bezpečnostní opatření v oblasti Zálivu. Politická nestabilita v Iráku a tlak na diplomatická řešení v Libanonu a Gaze budou nadále hýbat trhy.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further escalation of rhetoric between the US and Iran and heightened security measures in the Gulf region are expected. Political instability in Iraq and pressure for diplomatic solutions in Lebanon and Gaza will continue to move markets.
